correctness.rationale: The centralizer calculation is correct. For \(T=A[2]\), the center is exactly \(T\). Every \(a\in A\setminus T\) has centralizer \(A\), while \(a\gamma\) has centralizer \(T\cup aT\gamma\); two outside elements commute exactly when their \(A\)-coordinates differ by an element of \(T\). Hence the full commuting graph is \(K_t\vee(K_{m-t}\mathbin{\dot\cup}(m/t)K_t)\). The finite replay checks the multiplication law and edge relation on several kernels, but the universal result rests on the exact group calculation.

originality.rationale: The claimed graph decomposition is implication-covered by existing commuting-graph structure. Arvind, Ma, Cameron and Maslova prove for generalized dihedral groups with arbitrary abelian kernel that the center is the 2-torsion subgroup, the noncentral kernel is one clique, and the outside cosets split into cliques indexed by \(A/A[2]\); they also prove same-order isoclinic groups have isomorphic commuting graphs. The generalized dicyclic presentation changes only the central square of the outside generator, so its commutator/commuting predicate is the same as the corresponding generalized dihedral group. Thus the displayed decomposition, AC property, cograph/chordal conclusions, and dependence only on \((|A|,|A[2]|)\) follow routinely from the prior theorem plus this elementary observation.
